name: triage-route
description: Triage a work queue with one classifier node and the complementary two-gate branch pair: gates with negated `when` predicates and on_skip=prune route the run down exactly one arm (human escalation OR batch handling) and the dead arm's descendants never spawn. run_context seeds (ALL required): 'work_queue' = where the open items live (a file path, a command, or a URL your tools can read); 'action_target' = where routine actions are APPLIED (the ledger/ticket/file/CLI the rule's actions mutate — often the same place as work_queue, say so explicitly); 'decision_rule' = the owner's standing rule the classifier applies verbatim; 'owner_notify' = how a human is reached (a command, channel name, or file to write). PRUNE LAW (safety-bearing, earned in a two-estate clean-run): an arm node is skipped only when ALL its `after` deps are skipped — adding the classifier to an arm node's `after` 'for convenience' resurrects the dead arm and runs BOTH arms (the batch fan-out executed while the human still held the urgent gate). Therefore each arm hangs ONLY on its route-* gate and pulls the classifier payload via an explicit `inputs:` ref. The fan-out's items_from head must sit in its own `after`, so batch-prep (arm-scoped, hangs only on route-batch, pulls classify via `inputs:`) forwards the routine set — never point an arm node's `after` at the classifier itself. ROUTE SEMANTICS: the pair selects ONE arm per run — when urgent wins, routine items are NOT executed this lap (they stay in your queue; the report lists them for the owner to re-route next lap). RELEASE LAW: 'act' must name what is authorized; a bare 'act' executes nothing (proven: handle-urgent refuses and surfaces it). ADAPTER CONTRACT for work_queue: the intake node must be able to enumerate open items from it with whatever read-only tools the receiver has; nothing here mutates your tracker — every write/escalate step is a node you can point at your real system. Seeds are plain text: a seed value containing { or } breaks fan-out re-rendering and the launch refuses.

defaults.context:
You are one lane of a triage-route workflow. Ground rules:
- Read-only unless your node's goal explicitly says to act or escalate.
- Self-report is not proof: every classification cites the field or evidence in the item that drove it.
- Apply the owner's standing rule as written; do not invent policy. An item the rule does not clearly cover is 'ambiguous' — never force it into routine or urgent.
- Keep answers to the schema; one fenced ```json block as your final message. Never print secrets.

nodes.goal:
Classify every item from the intake payload (in ## Inputs) using the owner's standing rule, applied verbatim:
RULE: {run.decision_rule}
Buckets (an item goes in exactly one):
- routine: the rule says how to handle it AND no human judgment is needed
- urgent: the rule or its evidence says it must not wait for the batch
- ambiguous: the rule does not clearly cover it
Reply with ONLY fenced json {"has_urgent": true|false, "routine": [{"id": "<id>", "action": "<what the rule says to do>"}], "urgent": [{"id": "<id>", "evidence": "<why it must not wait>"}], "ambiguous": [{"id": "<id>", "why": "<the gap in the rule>"}], "rule_citations": "<one line: which part of the rule drove each bucket>"}
has_urgent MUST be true iff the urgent array is non-empty — the branch gates read that boolean (the gate grammar cannot see array length).

nodes.question: Urgent items need a human now — release which option?
nodes.context: Urgent set and evidence are in the classify output above (## Inputs). Owner-escalation channel: {run.owner_notify}. Escalation means surfacing the item to a human, not silently acting on it. Release law: 'act' must state WHAT is authorized (e.g. 'act: refund pw-101 up to $50') — a bare 'act' with no authorization is treated as not-approved by the executor.

nodes.goal:
Write the triage closeout from the payloads in ## Inputs. One arm will be absent — that is correct (the losing branch was pruned); say which arm ran. Cover: items seen, per-bucket counts, what was done per item with evidence, the ambiguous set the owner must rule on (list every one — they are the rule-gap backlog), and the gate answer if escalation ran.
Reply with ONLY fenced json {"lane": "urgent|batch", "seen": <int>, "done": ["<id: action + evidence>"], "ambiguous_for_owner": ["<id: the gap>"], "gate": "<released option + reason, or 'not reached'>"}
